newsitem.title: GREECE: Ship with illegal aliens was bound for Italy.
newsitem.headline: Ship with illegal aliens was bound for Italy.

text.p: Hundreds of mostly Kurdish illegal immigrants stranded on a ship that suffered a power failure in the Aegean Sea told Greek authorities on Thursday they had paid $2,000 each to be smuggled from Turkey to Italy.

Greece's Merchant Marine Ministry said the Ukrainian- registered ship Sohol, which suffered a power blackout in Greek waters at dawn on Wednesday, was carrying 303 illegal aliens including 26 children and 30 babies.
"The illegal aliens boarded the ship from the Turkish coast and were destined for Italy after paying $2,000 each," the ministry said in a statement.
Among the immigrants are 259 Iraqi and Turkish Kurds. The others come from Bangladesh, Morocco and Rwanda.
They lit fires in barrels on the deck to get help after the three-member Ukrainian crew abandoned the cargo ship which blacked out off the island of Andros, the ministry said.
The Sohol's captain told the immigrants that he was leaving to get them food but never returned. He had earlier told Greek authorities by radio to that his cargo was milk and rice destined for Italy.

Greek coastguard tug boats towed the Sohol off the coast near Athens, where investigators and doctors went aboard to examine the immigrants. One Rwandan was sent to hospital for treatment of a skin disease, the ministry said.
"Today we will begin the process of transporting them to special camps near Athens," a ministry official told Reuters.
Greek television showed scores of dishevelled men, women and children on deck, waving their arms and pieces of white cloth like flags at helicopters hovering above them.

Thousands of illegal immigrants are smuggled into Greece every year from the Third World, most paying thousands of dollars in passage fees. Many come by sea from Turkey and others cross Greece's rugged northern borders illegally.
Greek patrol boats ofter intercept Turkish boats, bringing mostly Iraqis and Kurds to Greek islands.

The extent of the illegal immigrant trade in the Mediterranean was made apparent last January after about 300 would-be immigrants were believed to have perished in a collision between smuggling boats off the coast of Sicily on Christmas Day.
The accident came to light after survivors smuggled into Greece told their story to the police.
